text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any neck pain or radiation of pain down your arm, and have you noticed any muscle wasting in your right shoulder or hand? I also need to ask if you have had any fevers, night sweats, or changes in your bowel or bladder habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest CT reveals a solid mass at the apex of your right lung, which is likely compressing the brachial plexus and causing your arm symptoms. Do you have any drooping of your right eyelid, a smaller pupil on the right side, or decreased sweating on the right side of your face? REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the lung mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal biopsy results, the presence of a solid mass at the lung apex combined with your arm symptoms is highly indicative of a Pancoast tumor. I will now request medical images to better visualize the tumor's extent and its impact on surrounding structures. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy result you provided is confusing, as a solid mass on CT should not yield normal readings unless it was a false negative or a sampling error. Given the classic presentation of a lung apex mass with brachial plexus symptoms, I am proceeding with the diagnosis of a Pancoast tumor despite the inconclusive biopsy.
